# edgeos_dhcp_server_settings (Resource)

The global DHCP server settings directly below `service dhcp-server`. There is only one set per router, so the resource takes over the existing values on create and the ID is always `dhcp-server`.

Only the attributes you set are managed. Attributes left unset are neither read nor changed, and removing an attribute from the configuration deletes the leaf, so EdgeOS uses its default again. Import reads every attribute. Shared networks below `shared-network-name` are never touched; manage them with `edgeos_dhcp_shared_network` and `edgeos_dhcp_static_mapping`.

Destroying the resource deletes the leaves it manages. EdgeOS then uses its defaults: the server is enabled, runs ISC dhcpd, and neither updates `/etc/hosts` nor adds static ARP entries.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "edgeos_dhcp_server_settings" "this" {
  disabled        = false
  hostfile_update = true
  static_arp      = false
  use_dnsmasq     = false
  global_parameters = [
    "option space ubnt;",
    "option ubnt.unifi-address code 1 = ip-address;",
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `disabled` (Boolean) Stop the DHCP server on every shared network (`disabled true`). EdgeOS default: `false`.
- `global_parameters` (List of String) Raw ISC dhcpd statements added to the top of `dhcpd.conf` (`global-parameters`), in order, such as `option space ubnt;`. Write double quotes as `&quot;`.
- `hostfile_update` (Boolean) Add the host names of DHCP clients to `/etc/hosts`, so the DNS forwarder resolves them (`hostfile-update enable`). EdgeOS default: `false`.
- `static_arp` (Boolean) Add permanent ARP entries for the static mappings (`static-arp enable`). EdgeOS default: `false`.
- `use_dnsmasq` (Boolean) Serve DHCP with dnsmasq instead of ISC dhcpd (`use-dnsmasq enable`). The raw dhcpd parameters (`global_parameters` and the `*_parameters` of shared networks) are ignored by dnsmasq. EdgeOS default: `false`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Always `dhcp-server`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = edgeos_dhcp_server_settings.this
  id = "dhcp-server"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import edgeos_dhcp_server_settings.example 'dhcp-server'
```
